headline: Load's spiked and sleep's short — today's Un1t class is about staying controlled, not chasing a number.
body_state: PaceForge's own readiness composite sits at 64.7 (moderate), driven by sleep — Garmin's own score reads 80/Productive, but that's before folding in load: acute:chronic ratio 1.98 (>1.5 carries 2–4x next-week injury risk) plus 21h of sleep debt over 14 days, only 6.1h logged last night (sleep score 71). Body battery is 42 this morning, HRV BALANCED at 47ms — not a red flag alone, but it isn't buying the debt back either. TSB -5.06 is still inside the productive -5…-30 band, so this isn't a shutdown day — it's a don't-add-to-the-pile day.
session: Today is Un1t (cross-training class, ~45 min, no structured targets set). Given the load spike and sleep debt, run it controlled: keep it in Z1/Z2 rather than the 130–148bpm grey zone your last few classes have sat in (Aug 1: 79.9% Z2/Z3, avg HR 130). Pick a lane — genuinely easy, or accept it as today's one harder stimulus and back off tomorrow's stacked easy run + Un1t Hyrox if body battery hasn't recovered by then.
recent: Yesterday's outdoor ride (28.8km, 513m climbing, 96min) was the right call — 146W avg, TE 1.6/0.0, genuinely easy despite the hills — but it's invisible to your training load right now (no HR, no power-TSS path for outdoor rides), so log an RPE on it. Monday's planned 4km easy+strides didn't happen, again. The Aug 1 cardio class (43min, avg HR 130, 79.9% Z2/Z3) repeats the grey-zone pattern flagged three reviews running — near-daily moderate cardio with no clear easy or hard lane.
focus: Rate yesterday's ride RPE — it's currently invisible to your training load.
Keep today's Un1t controlled — genuinely easy, or accept it as the day's one hard stimulus, not both.
Watch Wednesday: if body battery hasn't recovered, drop either the easy run or the Un1t Hyrox rather than stacking both.
